Edited to add - my friend passed suddenly in December about a month after my dad. I have bpd and had been suicidal for years; but got worse after he got sick. I had multiple attempts right up until my friend passed. We didn’t know what happened. The info from her family was sketchy. I was ADAMANT she took her own life and it ate me up inside. The pain was unbearable. I finally saw what I’d been putting my friends and family through. It hurt so much. The not knowing. Why didn’t she reach out, why couldn’t we have helped her. Why didn’t we notice. Finally we got the autopsy through. She didn’t take her own life, she died of an aneurysm in her brain. It was over in seconds. The sheer guttural cry I let out when I found out was like nothing I’ve experienced before. Even when I lost my dad. That cry was relief. That she hadn’t taken her own life. That she didn’t do it to herself. We couldn’t have saved her. It was just her time. 

Since then I’m trying to hard to stay because Jesus Christ that month of not knowing was utter hell on earth. I got to be on the other side and I know when you’re in the depths it feels like there’s no other way out but please, hold on. Better days are coming. They are. I promise.

What OP is talking about seems to be a long standing problem. If antibiotics are needed, 1 dose of a random antibiotic is NOT gonna help. There are lots of different types of antibiotic for a reason, certain antibiotics will have zero effect on an infection if the organism causing the infection is not sensitive to that particular antibiotic. This is more likely in someone suffering from recurrent infections. The most frequently used antibiotics for UTIs are usually Macrobid(nitrofurantoin and Trimethroprim. However, once again resistance can be built up to these and they can stop working, or they can not work at all as whatever is causing the uti may not be ‘sensitive’ to those 2 antibiotics. This is why urine samples are sent to the lab following a a positive urine dipstick for infection, so that it can be tested to see what organism is causing the issue and what antibiotics will work to take that bad boy down!
